source_rationale: The pancreas is a vital organ for maintaining metabolic homeostasis, consisting largely of exocrine ductal and acinar cells that produce and deliver digestive enzymes into the gut. Intermingled in the exocrine regions are the islets of Langerhans, comprised of at least five distinct endocrine cell types: α cells (secreting glucagon, GCG), β cells (insulin, INS), γ/PP cells (pancreatic polypeptide, PPY), δ cells (somatostatin, SST), and ε cells (ghrelin, GHRL), together making up less than 2% of pancreas mass.
